description: Five chest mistakes keep a skinny-fat chest flat no matter how many push-ups get done badly. Retest your strict push-up number, find your mistakes, and rebuild the chest signal with form that finally counts.

scenes.narration: Same test, new angle. | Front of the room. | Hands under shoulders. | One-minute timer. | Strict push-ups. | Film it if possible. | Chest to the floor. | Full lockout. | Count only clean reps. | That count is yours. | Write it down. | The front view exposes | what the side view hides. | Five mistakes live there. | At the end | I tell you | which ones are yours.

scenes.label: THE LINE YOUR FORM MUST DEFEND
scenes.narration: The line is the same as the season opener: twenty strict push-ups in a minute. What changes today is the audit. Last time we asked whether the signal exists. Today we ask how much of it your form actually delivers, because five mistakes tax every rep before the chest ever receives it. A man can own a twenty-five-rep test and a fifteen-rep chest, the missing ten reps paid out to his shoulders, his hips and the floor's momentum. Read your number, keep it in front of you through the list, and subtract honestly as we go. The verdict at the end uses the delivered number, not the performed one, and the delivered number is the one your mirror has been grading all along.
scenes.sub: performed number minus mistakes = delivered signal

scenes.narration: The root of all five mistakes is one fact: pressing is a team lift. The chest, front delts and triceps all push, and your nervous system pays whichever muscle shouts loudest. In most skinny-fat guys the delts and triceps have been shouting for years while the chest whispers, so default push-ups train the volunteers and starve the employee you actually hired. Form is how you reassign the work: hand position, elbow angle, body line and tempo decide which muscle receives the tension. That is why this episode exists. Your chest is not unresponsive. It is unassigned. Every mistake below is a specific way the assignment leaks to another muscle, and every fix is a specific way to route the tension home. Watch your front-view footage with that in mind and you will see your own leaks in the first ten reps, clear as subtitles. One more assignment leak hides in hand position, so check your footage for it. Hands drifting wider than your shoulders' comfortable line, or creeping in until the triceps take over, both reroute the paycheck before the set even starts. Set the hands under the outer chest, where the pec can actually shorten through the press, and keep them there for the whole set. Small geography, large salary difference.

Mistake one: the half rep. Stopping ten centimeters above the floor skips the exact range where the chest works hardest, the stretched bottom position, so the most valuable third of every rep is never performed. Mistake two: the broken line. Hips sagging or piked turn the push-up into a different, easier exercise and unload the chest at the very moment it should be carrying you. From the front you can see both instantly: elbows stopping early, hips drifting south. The fixes are unglamorous. Chest genuinely touches, every rep, even if the count drops by a third this week. And brace like a plank that happens to move: ribs down, glutes tight, one line from heels to head. Your number will fall before it rises. That fall is not regression. It is the first honest count of your life, and honest counts are the only ones that compound.

Mistake three: speed. Bouncing out of the bottom borrows elastic energy and momentum, and borrowed force is force the chest never produced, which means signal the chest never received. Two seconds down, a breath of pause, then press: the tempo tax disappears and the same set becomes a different exercise. Mistake four: shoulders leading the press. Watch the front footage: if your shoulders shrug toward your ears and roll forward at the top, your delts just collected the chest's paycheck again. Set the shoulders down and back before the first rep and keep them packed while you press, thinking about pushing the floor away rather than lifting yourself. The cue sounds backwards and works immediately. Your chest will feel the set in a place it has never felt it, which is how you know the assignment finally arrived at the right address.

beats.text: ADD A REP OR ADD A PAUSE

scenes.narration: Mistake five is the quietest: no progression. Doing the same fifteen reps the same way for three months sends a signal your chest fully adapted to by week four, and an adapted signal is background noise. Muscle grows when the instruction gets slightly louder over time: one more rep, a longer pause at the bottom, a slower negative, feet slightly higher. Small upgrades, applied weekly, are the entire progressive system. The light body helps you here more than anywhere: your joints tolerate the volume, your recovery clears fast, so you can progress some variable almost every session. Keep a notebook count, because progression you cannot see is progression you will not repeat. The plateau was never your genetics. It was a signal stuck on repeat, and repeat is a choice you can unmake this week.
Train with me, new rules. Four rounds, forty seconds of push-ups, two seconds down, chest to floor, twenty seconds of rest. Fewer reps, all of them delivered. Go.

beats.text: CHASING THE COUNT WITH FORM DEBT
SHRUGGING THE TOP OF EVERY REP

scenes.narration: The repair week, in order. Film one set from the front and grade it against the five mistakes before you change anything. Then rebuild the rep: two seconds down, a pause, shoulders packed, full lockout, for every working set this week. Expect the count to drop and welcome it. Progress exactly one variable next week, reps or pause length, never both, and write it down. The mistakes about the mistakes: chasing your old count with borrowed form, which reinstates every leak at once. And fixing all five in one session until the set becomes a thinking exercise with no tension in it. Fix one leak per week. In five weeks the same twenty reps will be a completely different signal, and your chest will file the difference where you can see it. One more grading rule for the film, so you judge it like a coach instead of a critic. Count a rep as delivered only if all three are true: the chest touched, the line stayed straight, and the shoulders stayed packed at the top. A set of ten with seven delivered is a seven-rep set wearing a costume. Write the delivered number in the log, because the log is where the next month's progression gets calculated from, and progression calculated from fiction produces fiction at scale.

scenes.label: THEN WE RETEST FROM THE FRONT
scenes.narration: So, your delivered number. If the front view showed three or more mistakes, your chest has been training at half salary, and the five-week repair is the highest-value work in your program right now. If you saw one or two, fix them in order and watch the same count transform. If your set was clean, your signal is fully delivered and load progression is your only remaining lever. Put your delivered number in the comments, the honest count after subtracting your leaks. Just the number. In thirty days we retest from the front, and the footage will grade your chest signals better than your memory ever will.
scenes.sub: half salary / repairing / fully delivered - film the truth

title: 5 skinny fat chest Mistakes That Are Destroying Your chest muscle signals
